# CANDIDATE: VOLATILITY_COMPRESSION_NAMED_LEVEL_REJECTION

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When ATR contracts sharply near a named level (prior day high/low), price often respects that level, providing a reversal signal. This edge exists because low volatility indicates reduced momentum and increased likelihood of mean reversion at significant structural levels, particularly during low-VIX midday sessions when named levels act as magnet.

## Mechanism

Calculate ATR(10). If current ATR < 0.5 × 20-day average ATR (contraction). Simultaneously, if price is within 0.1% of prior day’s high (for short) or low (for long). Look for a reversal candle: for short near prior day high, a bearish engulfing or shooting star (close < open, upper wick > 2×body); for long near prior day low, bullish engulfing or hammer (close > open, lower wick > 2×body). Enter at close of reversal candle. Exit shape: Chart‑stop at the named level ±0.2% as buffer, TP1 at 1.5R, runner using chandelier trail (ATR×2.5). Regime hint: Ideal during low VIX (<15) and midday (11:00‑14:00 EST) when named levels are respected; avoid high volatility expansion periods.
